exhibit-1.summary: The economics table has the price Hollis Bay receives per bag, each variable cost per bag, the first-year launch costs and the recipe development cost.

exhibit-2.summary: The survey table has shoppers' purchase intent at the shelf price, what they like most and what makes them hesitate, with the planning assumptions from past launches.

exhibit-3.summary: The proposal table describes the in-store sampling program: what it is, its cost, and the extra buying households and bags it is expected to bring.

definitions.text: Variable cost per bag is the ingredients, packaging, roasting labor and energy, and freight for one bag: the costs that rise with every bag made.
Contribution per bag is the price Hollis Bay receives from retailers, not the shelf price shoppers pay, less the variable cost per bag.
First-year launch costs are the roasting line, marketing and advertising, and shelf fees; the recipe development was spent last year and is left out.
Break-even volume is the first-year launch costs divided by the contribution per bag.

The buying share is the share of households who actually buy in year one: each purchase-intent answer's share of shoppers times its conversion rate from the planning assumptions, added up over the answers that convert.
Buying households are the households that shop in stores carrying Hollis Bay times the buying share.
Year-one bags are the buying households times the bags each buying household buys in year one.
Year-one profit is the bags sold beyond the break-even volume times the contribution per bag: total contribution less the first-year launch costs.

definitions.term: bags per household to break even
definitions.text: The bags each buying household must buy to break even are the break-even volume divided by the buying households.
Extra bags from sampling are the extra buying households the proposal expects times the bags each of them buys, on top of the survey-based forecast.
The net gain from sampling is the extra bags times the contribution per bag, less the program cost, which comes on top of the launch costs.

definitions.term: bags to cover the sampling cost
definitions.text: The bags needed to cover the sampling cost are the program cost divided by the contribution per bag.
